tasks.short: Answer questions, apply contracts, and sort out problems between managers and employees

today.trigger: A manager or employee writes, calls, or stops the HR business partner on the floor about a contract, the roster, pay, or a conflict.
steps: Read the message and find the person in AFAS Profit: contract, hours, site, and which CAO applies.
Search SharePoint, old mail, and the CAO text for the clause that fits.
Talk with the manager and the employee, often separately and often more than once.
Decide what the company will do and write a file note.
If pay or the contract must change, pass that to the HR administrator or the payroll specialist.
drudgery: Retelling the same leave, overtime, and contract-hour rules
Hunting SharePoint and mail for the current version of a policy
Rewriting a file note that says the same thing as the last one
today.time_sinks: The long part is finding the clause and retelling it. The conversation is long only when two people are actually in conflict.

lenses.faster: Repeat questions on leave, overtime, and contract hours get a cited reply and leave the HR business partner's day. A conflict or a contract change still takes the same conversations it takes now, plus a short read of the case brief, so about a third of this task's time goes.
lenses.autonomous: A message in the HR Teams channel or shared mailbox starts it. A front door answers from the approved policies and CAO texts when the question is general, and opens a case when a person, a sanction, or a contract is named. The HR business partner is the gate on every one of those cases.
lenses.ambitious: Night-shift supervisors in Rotterdam, Tilburg, and Venlo get a cited first answer, and a case opened, while their shift is still on. Demand would grow: site managers would want the same for weekend crews and, with the three agencies, for flex leads in the months when flex headcount rises.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss searching SharePoint and old mail for the current leave rule. The work they want more of is the conversation where a manager and an employee disagree and still have to work the next shift together.
lenses.options: Two readings of the same clause, one holding the rule and one granting an exception, with the hours and the team effect of each, change what the manager decides to do.
lenses.altitude: The week starts from a list of open cases instead of an inbox of rule questions. They gain the decision on which cases they take and which clause readings the front door may send on its own. The job becomes more expert, centred on disputes and contract changes.
reach: The HR administrator's first answer on which contract clause applies, once the HR business partner can read the AFAS contract and use the administrator's checklist of what must be in writing before a change.

tasks.human_edge: The HR business partner can hear what someone will not put in a message, judge whether the manager's account is fair, and keep two people working together the next morning. A cited clause cannot do that.
tasks.pattern_why: A message may be a rule, a contract reading, or a dispute, and that is not known until it is read, so the path cannot be fixed in advance. A personal outcome counts only after the HR business partner decides; a general answer counts only when it quotes a text they have already cleared.

in_practice.trigger: A message arrives in the HR Teams channel or the shared HR mailbox.
steps: Classify it as a general rule or as a matter about a named person, a contract, pay, or a conflict.
For a general rule, reply from the approved SharePoint policies and CAO texts, cite the paragraph and the version date, and say the reply is from AI.
For a named person or a conflict, open a case for the HR business partner with the question and the cited clause. Do not open AFAS.
The HR business partner pulls the contract and hours from AFAS, talks with the people, and decides.
The HR administrator or the payroll specialist changes AFAS only after that decision.
in_practice.human_gate: Every case about a named person, every contract or pay change, and every question the approved texts do not cover. General answers go out only on topics and documents the HR business partner has already cleared.
data_needed: Versioned house policies and both CAO texts, with the topics the front door may answer
The incoming message
AFAS contract, hours, and site, pulled by the HR business partner after a case is opened
in_practice.logs_to: The HR case list on SharePoint: the question, the clause cited, whether an answer was sent or a case was opened, and who decided the outcome.

evidence.claim: IBM's Ask HR takes manager and employee questions at scale and escalates complex cases to HR business partners, who are the first human level of support; phone and email support were removed to drive use. The reported saving on that support is about 40 percent and is self-reported.
evidence.source: IBM Ask HR, Cornell CAHRS HRBP Exchange, 12 May 2026, https://www.ilr.cornell.edu/sites/default/files-d8/2026-05/hrbp-exchange-final.pdf

evidence.claim: Coca-Cola Andina's HR agent serves about 1,200 of 3,600 staff in a typical month, with a CSAT of 4.1, and raises a ticket for what it cannot answer.
evidence.source: Coca-Cola Andina HR support, Microsoft Learn, 8 Sep 2026, https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-platform/guidance/case-studies/coca-cola-andina-hr-support

evidence.claim: A Dutch works council must consent before AI that processes personnel data or can observe behaviour or performance is introduced (WOR art. 27(1)(k) and (l)).
Danish HR professionals using chatbots saved about 3 percent of their hours, so a large saving on this inbox is a local fact to measure, not a default.

risks: An answer quoted from an old SharePoint file becomes the practice on a night shift before anyone corrects it.
Letting the front door open AFAS before the works council has consented breaches WOR art. 27 and AVG purpose limits.
Staff must be told the first reply is AI (EU AI Act art. 50). A manager can treat a drafted reply as the company's decision in a dispute.
research_questions: Over four weeks, what share of this inbox is a repeat rule with no named person, and what share is a dispute or a contract change?
Will the works council consent to a front door that only quotes policy, and is consent a separate question once it can open an AFAS contract?
Do night-shift supervisors in Rotterdam, Tilburg, and Venlo use Teams, or do they still phone the day HR business partner?
How many of last month's replies would have been wrong if they had quoted the current SharePoint text?

tasks.short: Explain the CAO, HR policies, and the rules a manager has to follow

today.trigger: A manager or employee asks what the rule is, or a case needs a clause checked before someone acts.
steps: Hear the question and restate it in concrete terms, such as overtime, probation, leave, or a required certificate.
Find the current policy on SharePoint or the matching article in the transport CAO or the warehouse CAO.
Explain it in plain language, including what it means for that site and that shift.
Where the person's own contract matters, check AFAS and say how the rule applies.
Point them to the HR administrator or payroll when a record has to change.
drudgery: Repeating probation, leave, overtime, and certificate rules several times a day
Checking which PDF is the current one
Rewriting the same answer for each manager
today.time_sinks: The lookup and the rewriting take most of the time. The rare question where two rules conflict is the short part.

lenses.faster: Finding the current text and rewriting the standard answer disappear for every question the approved documents cover. A clash between texts, or a question about a named person, still takes a sitting as it does today, plus a sample check of what was sent, and together that is under half of this task.
lenses.autonomous: A question in Teams or the HR mailbox starts it. The workflow matches the current policy or CAO text, drafts a short quoted answer, and sends it when the question is general and the match is clear. The HR business partner is the gate when the texts clash, a person is named, or the match is weak.
lenses.ambitious: A new service to the works council: each month, the clauses staff actually asked about, so the council can see where the CAO and house practice diverge. Demand would grow if that list were cheap; the council and the HR director would want it per site, not once a year.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss retyping the probation and overtime answers. The work they want more of is the case where the CAO and the warehouse scheme do not say the same thing.
lenses.options: When two clauses could apply, showing both readings with the pay effect of each changes whether the manager treats the hours as overtime or as a shift change.
lenses.altitude: Rule repetition leaves the week. They gain the decision to withdraw a document from the answer set when it is no longer the rule payroll uses, and to overrule a reading when the CAO and the house scheme clash. The job becomes more expert on those clashes.
reach: The payroll specialist's explanation to a manager of how a CAO allowance is built up, once the HR business partner knows the wage-component codes. The payroll specialist keeps the month close.

tasks.human_edge: When the written rule and the site's practice disagree, or a manager wants cover the text does not give, the HR business partner has to say what the company will stand behind. A quoted paragraph cannot make that call.
tasks.pattern_why: Each general question follows the same path: match the current policy or CAO text, quote it, and send, or hand it over when the match is weak or a person is named. One model call inside that fixed path is enough.

in_practice.trigger: A policy question arrives in the HR mailbox or the HR Teams channel.
steps: Match the question to the current SharePoint policy or to the transport or warehouse CAO, using the version date.
Draft a short answer that quotes the paragraph.
Send it when the question is general and the match is clear, with a line that the answer is from AI.
Route named-person questions, clashes between texts, and weak matches to the HR business partner with the draft and the quotes attached.
When an answer was wrong, the HR business partner corrects the source document, not only the reply.
in_practice.human_gate: Clashing texts, any named person, anything about dismissal or pay, and a weekly sample of answers that were sent. The HR business partner clears the document set before anything is sent automatically.
data_needed: Versioned house policies and both CAO texts
A list of topics the workflow may answer without a person
The question itself, without the employee's performance or absence history
in_practice.logs_to: A log of the question, the sources cited, whether it was sent or escalated, and any correction by the HR business partner, kept for the works council.

evidence.claim: An HR agent over owned content already answers staff questions at Coca-Cola Andina and passes on what it cannot answer.
IBM runs a company front door for HR questions and keeps HR business partners for the cases that escalate. The 40 percent saving is self-reported.
People must be told they are interacting with AI (EU AI Act art. 50). AI that evaluates performance or influences promotion or termination is high-risk from 2 December 2027 (Annex III, point 4(b)).
HR staff report that access to personal data and IT sign-off decide what they may use, and that many firms allow a generative tool only for email.

risks: The house scheme and the CAO disagree, and the reply quotes only the file that happens to be on SharePoint.
IT sign-off that allows a generative tool only for email stops a Teams front door before it starts.
One corpus misleads if Venlo, Tilburg, and Rotterdam do not apply the rule in the same way.
Using a person's absence or performance record in the answer moves the tool toward high-risk evaluation from 2 December 2027.
research_questions: Are the SharePoint policies dated and complete, and do they match the rules the payroll specialist uses for both CAOs?
On a blind set of 50 real questions, how many quoted answers are right, and what error rate will the HR director accept before answers go out unreviewed?
Does the works council treat a policy bot that holds no personal data as needing consent under WOR art. 27?
Which common questions have a different answer in Rotterdam, Tilburg, and Venlo?

tasks.short: Match people to teams, shifts, and sites under CAO and certificate rules

today.trigger: A manager asks to fill a seat or change a shift, a certificate is about to lapse, or peak season needs more hands.
steps: See who is on the team in AFAS: contract, hours, site, and end date.
Check Studytube for a valid forklift, VCA, or food-safety certificate.
Ask the manager who they want and who the roster cannot spare.
Check CAO limits on hours, notice, and a temporary move between sites.
Propose a match. If the person is a flex worker, the order goes through one of the three agency portals.
drudgery: Copying certificate dates and contract hours into a spreadsheet
Chasing the three agencies for who is still available
Rebuilding the same overview at every peak
today.time_sinks: The spreadsheet takes longer than the decision. The decision waits on late data, not on a long meeting.

lenses.faster: Building the spreadsheet of contracts, hours, and certificates disappears. The talk with the manager about who moves stays at its present length, and it is most of this task, so about a third of the time goes.
lenses.autonomous: A manager's request, or a weekly check that a certificate or a contract ends inside the planning window, starts it. Software prepares who meets the written rules on certificate, contract, site, and hours. Nobody is moved until the HR business partner and the manager agree, and a person still places any agency order.
lenses.ambitious: Each site decides every week who must come off a shift, or book a renewal, before a forklift, VCA, or food-safety certificate lapses, instead of discovering it after the shift is already unlawful to run. Demand would grow in peak season, when lapses and flex cover pile up together.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss maintaining the certificate spreadsheet. The work they want more of is the talk with a manager about whether a crew can carry a move.
lenses.options: Three feasible options for the same seat, a permanent move, a longer flex booking, or waiting for a renewal, with the cost and the CAO limit of each, change which one the manager picks. Today there is time to build only one.
lenses.altitude: Monday starts with an eligibility view per site instead of a fresh spreadsheet. They gain the decision to refuse a move that breaks hours, certificate, or contract rules, with the facts already on the page. The job becomes more expert on team fit and on those constraints.
reach: The learning and development specialist's chase of forklift, VCA, and food-safety expiries for people already on the roster, once the HR business partner can read Studytube completion and expiry. The specialist keeps the courses.

tasks.human_edge: Two people with the same valid certificate can still be the wrong pair on a tight crew, and a manager's preferred name can be a favourite. That call stays with the HR business partner and the manager, on facts, without a score.
tasks.pattern_why: Who is allowed to do the work follows written rules on certificate, contract, and hours. Who actually moves is a judgment about that crew, and the HR business partner stays the lead so a model is never asked to rank people.

in_practice.trigger: A manager asks to fill or change a seat, or a weekly check shows a certificate or a contract end inside the planning window.
steps: Pull contract, site, hours, and valid certificates for the people who could do the work.
Apply the written rules and set aside anyone who fails certificate, contract type, site, or CAO hours.
Draft two or three feasible options and the constraint each one uses.
The HR business partner and the manager choose.
A person places any agency order and any AFAS change.
in_practice.human_gate: Every assignment. The draft contains no rank on performance, absence, or inferred traits. The HR business partner and the manager sign the choice.
data_needed: Contract type, hours, site, and end date from AFAS
Certificate status and expiry from Studytube
The shift's required certificates and the CAO hours limits
Agency availability for flex cover
in_practice.logs_to: A short note on the team file: the option chosen and the written rule that set someone aside, so the works council can see the basis.

evidence.claim: From 2 December 2027, AI that allocates tasks based on behaviour or personal traits is high-risk, and the employer then needs a competent overseer, logs, and must inform workers' representatives first.
evidence.source: EU AI Act Annex III, point 4(b), and article 26, https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/annex/3/ and https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/article/26/

evidence.claim: Works-council consent is required before a system that processes personnel data or can observe behaviour or performance.
Microsoft's Workforce Insights agent shows managers structure and staffing without having to ask HR.
A vendor contract does not move the employer's duty for a tool that affects people at work.

risks: Ranking on absence, speed, or a trait makes this high-risk allocation from 2 December 2027 and needs works-council consent now.
A late Studytube date can clear someone for a forklift the shift lead knows has lapsed.
Flex workers are employed by the agency. A Noordhaven file that scores them mixes two employers.
Managers can treat a draft list as an order and move someone before the HR business partner has agreed.
research_questions: Can the real constraints be written down as certificate, contract type, CAO hours, and site, or does the choice depend on facts only the manager holds?
How often does Studytube disagree with the paper certificate the shift lead trusts?
Will the works council accept a list that excludes someone from a move when it contains no performance or absence score?
What share of these requests is an agency order rather than an internal move?

tasks.short: Advise managers on filling roles and on who is still here after 90 days

today.trigger: A site has roles open too long, a team is losing new hires, or the quarterly review with the HR director is due.
steps: Pull open roles, stage times, and offer outcomes from Recruitee.
Pull starters, leavers, and who is still employed at day 90 from AFAS.
Ask the recruiter and the manager what they think is going wrong.
Draft a short note with where to recruit and what to change in week one.
Discuss it with the manager and agree what they will do before the next review.
drudgery: Rebuilding funnel and leaver numbers by hand for each site
Chasing the recruiter for interview notes sitting in Recruitee
Formatting the same note again for the management team
today.time_sinks: Getting a picture of one team that the manager trusts takes longer than the advice conversation.

lenses.faster: Hand-building the Recruitee funnel, the AFAS starter and leaver list, and the day-90 figures disappears. The advice meeting stays at its present length, and about two fifths of this task's time goes.
lenses.autonomous: A new vacancy that runs past the site's usual time to hire, a day-90 exit, or the monthly site date starts it. A draft pack is assembled from Recruitee and the nightly AFAS extract. Nothing is sent to the manager as HR's advice until the HR business partner has signed it.
lenses.ambitious: Each warehouse manager gets a monthly decision on their own starters: still here at day 90, and whether onboarding was finished in week one. Today that decision sits in a quarterly company slide. Demand would grow; the three site managers would ask for the same pack for their team leads once it is cheap to produce.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss rebuilding the Recruitee and leaver tables. The work they want more of is the meeting where a manager commits to a change in week one or in how the team is staffed.
lenses.options: Three readings of the same exits, pay, roster, and the manager's own behaviour, each with the evidence for it, change whether the action is a roster fix, a pay check with the compensation and benefits specialist, or a conversation with the manager.
lenses.altitude: One standing meeting per site replaces the scramble before the quarterly review. They gain the decision to put a team on the HR director's list when day-90 retention falls through a line agreed in advance. The job becomes more expert on causes.
reach: The recruiter's account of why offers were lost and which Recruitee stage is slow, once the HR business partner knows the pipeline and the offer steps. The recruiter keeps the candidates and the search.

tasks.human_edge: A manager will say more about why people leave in the room than an exit code in AFAS records. The HR business partner has to judge which cause is real and which action that manager will actually carry out.
tasks.pattern_why: The numbers can be assembled the same way each month, but the advice depends on what that manager will do on that shift. The HR business partner stays the lead; the draft pack only shortens the preparation.

in_practice.trigger: Month start, a day-90 exit, or a role open longer than the site's usual time to hire.
steps: Refresh a one-page pack from Recruitee and the nightly AFAS extract: time to hire, offer acceptance, week-one onboarding, still employed at day 90, and absence.
Draft three possible readings and the action each reading implies.
The HR business partner checks the numbers with the recruiter and drops any reading the data does not support.
The HR business partner and the manager agree one action.
The action, the owner, and the date are written down for the next month.
in_practice.human_gate: The recommendation itself, and any sharing of named people's exit reasons outside the HR file. The manager sees team figures, not candidate notes.
data_needed: Vacancy stages, time in stage, and offer outcomes from Recruitee
Starter and leaver dates, site, and team from AFAS
Week-one onboarding completion
Exit reasons only under the existing retention purpose, shown at a level that does not identify a person
in_practice.logs_to: The monthly site note on the HR SharePoint: the figures, the reading chosen, the action, and the owner.

evidence.claim: At Workday, an HR business partner's calibration agent was called super useful by 83 percent of HR business partners, and half of them cut preparation time by up to 75 percent. The business result after the build was hard to prove. This is a vendor reporting on itself.
A manager-facing staffing view can show structure and staffing without a request to HR.
Across Danish HR professionals, chatbot use saved about 3 percent of hours, so less preparation does not by itself move retention.

risks: Exit text tied to a named manager becomes an evaluation of that manager, which is high-risk from 2 December 2027 and needs works-council consent.
A small team at one site can be identified from a leaving reason even with the name removed, which breaches AVG.
Recruitee holds candidate data the warehouse manager should not see.
Preparation can shrink while day-90 retention does not move, which is the result Workday could not show after a similar build.
research_questions: Are time to hire, offer acceptance, week-one onboarding, and day-90 retention stored as fields in Recruitee and AFAS, or rebuilt in Excel each quarter?
For last year's day-90 leavers, was the cause already visible in data the HR business partner had in week two?
Looking at the last four quarterly reviews, did the site managers change a hiring or onboarding decision because of the pack?
Can exit reasons be shown at team level at Venlo, the smallest site, without identifying a person?

tasks.short: Coach managers on interviews, reviews, and writing down performance problems

today.trigger: A manager has to interview, hold a review, start a counseling talk, or write down a performance problem.
steps: Hear what the manager wants to do and how soon.
Explain the company way to interview, review, or document, including what a later dismissal file has to contain for UWV or the kantonrechter.
Find a SharePoint template or an old example that is safe to copy from.
Practice the conversation with the manager.
Read the note they actually wrote before it goes on the employee's file.
drudgery: Hunting for the last good example of a warning or a review form
Turning a manager's messy notes into a dated timeline
Repeating the same interview briefing for every new team lead
today.time_sinks: The practice conversation is the work. The sink before it is finding the example and cleaning the notes so the conversation can start.

lenses.faster: Searching for a template and turning messy notes into a dated timeline disappear. The practice session, and the check of the note the manager wrote, stay at their present length, and they are about three quarters of this task.
lenses.autonomous: A manager's request, or a new team lead's first review cycle, starts it. A practice outline and a timeline of facts already on the file are drafted before the session. The HR business partner runs the session, and only a person puts a note on the employee's file.
lenses.ambitious: Night-shift and weekend team leads, who now get no coaching because the three HR business partners work days, get one practice session before their first review or their first warning. Demand would grow: there are more team leads than those three can sit with, and cheaper preparation means the sessions get requested instead of skipped.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss hunting for a sample letter. The work they want more of is the live practice where a manager finds their own words for a hard talk.
lenses.options: Two openings for the same situation, a coaching talk or a formal note that starts a file, change what the manager decides to do. The choice is the decision. The wording effort is secondary.
lenses.altitude: More of the week is practice sessions with team leads, including those on shifts. They gain the decision to refuse a warning or a review note that would not stand in a dismissal file. The job becomes more expert on the conversation and on the file.
reach: The recruiter's briefing of a hiring manager on the structured interview and on how to write feedback in Recruitee, once the HR business partner knows that scorecard. The recruiter keeps the vacancy and the candidate.

tasks.human_edge: The HR business partner can tell when a manager is not ready to hold the talk, and can stop a note that would fail at UWV or the kantonrechter. A smooth draft in the manager's place is something employees notice and pull back from. The person owns the file.
tasks.pattern_why: The conversation cannot be scripted before the manager speaks, and the employee has to hear the manager's own words. The HR business partner stays the lead. The draft is preparation for the session, and it is not the document that goes to the employee.

in_practice.trigger: A manager asks for help before an interview, a review, a counseling talk, or a warning.
steps: Pull the SharePoint template and, where a file already exists, a timeline of dated facts from AFAS and the written notes.
Draft a practice outline as prompts the manager can try, not as text they should send.
The HR business partner runs the practice session. The manager speaks in their own words.
The manager writes the note.
The HR business partner checks it before it is stored and sends back anything the manager cannot evidence.
in_practice.human_gate: The session, the decision to open a formal file, and every document stored on the employee. No drafted text is sent to the employee as the manager's feedback. Practice uses text only, with no reading of face or voice.
data_needed: The company templates for interviews, reviews, and warnings
Dated facts already on the employee's file
The manager's own notes of what happened
in_practice.logs_to: The employee file holds the manager's signed note and the fact that the HR business partner checked it. The practice draft is not stored on the employee's record.

evidence.claim: Managers who draft feedback with AI report that employees can tell and that most then seem more closed off.
Workday's check-in agent raised the share of write-ups marked Good by 16 points, against 7 points for non-users, on 12,200 write-ups. This is a vendor reporting on its own HR team.
Inferring emotions from face or voice at work is prohibited. AI that evaluates performance is high-risk from 2 December 2027.
evidence.source: EU AI Act art. 5(1)(f) and Annex III, point 4(b), https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/article/5/ and https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/annex/3/

evidence.claim: A Dutch dismissal needs a documented file for UWV or the kantonrechter. A model may draft a timeline from existing records; a person owns the file.

risks: A manager sends the draft anyway, and the employee pulls back from the talk.
A voice practice tool that scores emotion is banned under EU AI Act art. 5(1)(f).
A polished timeline can hide a missing fact, and the file then fails at UWV or the kantonrechter. The employer keeps that duty.
Storing practice drafts on the employee record is personnel data and needs works-council consent under WOR art. 27.
research_questions: Do Noordhaven managers want a practice session, or do they want HR to write the note for them?
In the last warning and dismissal files, which required facts were missing, and were those facts already in AFAS?
Will a team lead on nights attend a coaching session if it is offered inside their shift?
Has AI-written feedback already reached Noordhaven employees, and what did they do when they noticed?

tasks.short: Set up how staff raise grievances and how satisfaction is checked

today.trigger: The yearly survey is due, a cluster of complaints appears at a site, or the works council asks for a pulse.
steps: Agree with the HR director and the works council what will be asked and who will see the answers.
Pick a channel warehouse staff will use. Many do not sit at a desk, so mail alone fails.
Run it on the shifts that can be reached, then read the comments by hand.
Decide what is a grievance to handle and what is a theme to report.
Tell the works council what was done with the result.
drudgery: Chasing responses from people who are on a shift, not at a desk
Coding free-text comments by hand
Rewriting the question set from scratch each time a site asks for a small change
today.time_sinks: Getting a fair response from the shifts, then reading the free text. The meetings with the works council are slow, and they have to stay that way.

lenses.faster: Hand-coding a pile of old comments into themes gets shorter, as a draft the HR business partner checks. The design meetings with the works council and the HR director stay as they are, and they are most of this task, so about a quarter of the time goes.
lenses.autonomous: The annual cycle, a works-council request, or a site problem the current survey does not see starts a design cycle. A draft question set and a sample grouping of last year's comments are prepared for the meeting. The works council's consent comes before any new channel is switched on, and the HR business partner decides what counts as a grievance.
lenses.ambitious: Night shift at the three sites, and flex workers on the floor, get a grievance route that a named person answers. They are barely present in today's office survey. Demand would grow in the months when agency headcount moves from about 150 toward 300, because site managers will want that route while the extra people are there.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss hand-coding comments. The work they want more of is the works-council discussion about what will change, and closing a grievance with the person who raised it.
lenses.options: Two designs, a short pulse on roster and safety, or a full satisfaction survey, change what management is then obliged to answer and what the works council will consent to. That is a different decision, not a shorter meeting.
lenses.altitude: This work becomes a few design sessions a year plus a watch on whether grievances were answered. They gain, with the works council, the decision on what a channel may ask, and the decision on which comments are grievances. The job becomes more expert on employee voice and on the council's consent.
reach: The people-analytics analyst's first grouping of survey comments, once the HR business partner knows which fields in that model must not be joined to a person. The analyst keeps the dataset and the nightly refresh.

tasks.human_edge: Deciding whether a comment is a complaint the company must act on, a signal about a manager, or something else, and whether a question will get a warehouse worker into trouble with their supervisor. That judgment stays with the HR business partner.
tasks.pattern_why: The method has to be agreed with the works council and has to fit how a shift actually speaks up. A draft question set and a sample coding help the meeting. The HR business partner owns the design, so an open-ended agent is the wrong shape.

in_practice.trigger: The annual cycle, a request from the works council, or a site problem the current survey does not reach.
steps: Draft a short question set aimed at one gap, such as night shift, and try it on last year's comments as a sample only.
Check the draft against AVG purpose limitation and against the ban on inferring emotion from face or voice.
Put the design to the works council before anything is switched on.
After consent, run a pilot on one site and one shift, on a channel the shift can open at work.
The HR business partner decides which comments are grievances and who answers the person.
in_practice.human_gate: Works-council consent before go-live. The HR business partner reviews every comment that names a person or alleges unfair treatment. No score is stored against an employee.
systems: a form that opens on a shared warehouse terminal
data_needed: The consented question set
Comments from that set, with site and shift
Headcount by shift so a small crew is not treated as a result
A separate route for flex workers that does not copy agency personnel files into AFAS
in_practice.logs_to: The works-council file: the design, the consent, the response rate by site and shift, and what was done with the themes. Grievances follow the existing complaint procedure.

evidence.claim: Works-council consent is required before AI that processes personnel data or can observe behaviour or performance, and councils are often brought in only after go-live.
The Dutch Social and Economic Council advises that people affected by an AI outcome must always be able to complain.
Inferring emotion from face or voice at work is prohibited. Text sentiment on workplace messages is not biometric, but it is monitoring and needs consent.
evidence.source: EU AI Act art. 5(1)(f), https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/article/5/ ; consent point is model knowledge, stated as such in the role digest

evidence.claim: Text sentiment on workplace chat is monitoring and needs consent. This is a reading of the law, not a court ruling.

risks: A sentiment score on comments is monitoring of behaviour and needs works-council consent. Asking the council after go-live is the known failure.
People affected by a theme need a way to complain, which the SER advice treats as required.
A low response on nights is read as satisfaction if nobody checks who never saw the form.
Flex-worker answers stored in AFAS treat Noordhaven as their employer. The agency is the employer.
research_questions: What was the response rate of the last survey on day shift versus night shift, by site?
What has the works council refused or delayed on the last two technology requests?
Do the three agencies already run a complaint channel for flex workers that Noordhaven should feed rather than copy?
Can a pilot in one hall group comments without storing a score against a person's name?

tasks.short: Prepare the satisfaction report and the presentation for management

today.trigger: A survey has closed, or the management team or the works council meets and expects the figures.
steps: Export the scores from Excel or from the Power BI HR dashboard.
Read the comments and tag themes by hand.
Build the charts and write the slide story in PowerPoint.
Add what HR recommends management do.
Present it and answer the questions in the room.
drudgery: Refreshing numbers the nightly AFAS extract already holds
Hand-tagging comments
Rebuilding last year's slides with new numbers
today.time_sinks: Comment coding and slide formatting take the hours. The meeting is shorter, and it is where the argument happens.

lenses.faster: Exporting numbers that are already in Power BI, and hand-tagging comments into a slide story, disappear. Editing the draft and presenting it stay, together about two fifths of the effort this task takes today.
lenses.autonomous: Survey close, or ten days before the management-team or works-council meeting, starts it. Power BI refreshes the scores from the nightly extract, and one pass groups the consented comments into themes with quotes. The HR business partner approves the pack before anyone else sees it.
lenses.ambitious: Each site manager gets that site's own pack in the week the survey closes, split by shift, and decides what to fix before the next peak. Today they share one company presentation. Demand would grow: Tilburg and Venlo would want their own pack each time, not only a Rotterdam story once a year.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss formatting the slides. The work they want more of is the management meeting where the figures force a decision.
lenses.options: Two readings of the same scores, workload and roster on one side and leadership at a site on the other, with the comments behind each, lead the management team to different actions. A single company average hides that choice.
lenses.altitude: Slide production leaves the week. They gain the decision to hold back a pack that would identify a small crew, and the decision on which reading goes to the management team. The job becomes more expert on interpretation.
reach: The people-analytics analyst's written commentary on the HR dashboard, once the HR business partner knows which measures in the nightly AFAS extract are safe to quote. The analyst keeps the model and the refresh.

tasks.human_edge: The HR business partner has to cut a quote that identifies a small night crew, and has to defend a figure the management team dislikes. A fluent paragraph will not make either call.
tasks.pattern_why: The scores already follow a fixed Power BI dashboard on the nightly extract. The messy part is the comments, and one pass can turn them into themes a person checks against the quotes. The steps are the same each quarter.

in_practice.trigger: The survey closes, or the management-team or works-council date is ten days away.
steps: Refresh the Power BI scores from the nightly AFAS extract and the survey file.
Group the consented comments into themes and attach three quotes to each theme.
Draft a short narrative with two possible readings and no ranking of named people.
The HR business partner checks every quote, removes anything that would identify a small team, and cuts any theme the quotes do not support.
The HR business partner approves the pack and presents it.
in_practice.human_gate: Every pack before it is sent or shown. A theme is shown only after the HR business partner has compared it with the quotes and hidden small cells.
data_needed: Consented survey scores and comments
Headcount by site and shift, so small cells can be hidden
The measure definitions already used in the nightly AFAS dashboard
in_practice.logs_to: The SharePoint folder shared with the works council: the pack, the date, who approved it, and which cells were hidden.

evidence.claim: Managers can be given structure and staffing from a workforce view without asking HR to build the pack each time.
A people-review aid can cut preparation sharply and still leave the later business result unproven. Workday reported this about its own HR team.
People affected by an AI outcome must have a way to complain.
Danish HR chatbot use saved about 3 percent of hours on average, so this task can shrink while the HR business partner's week barely moves.

risks: A quote identifies a small night crew at Venlo even with the name removed, which breaches AVG.
Joining survey text to performance or absence data turns the pack into an evaluation tool, high-risk from 2 December 2027.
A fluent narrative overstates a theme the quotes do not support, and the management team acts on it.
If a person is acted on because of the pack, they need a route to complain, as the SER advice requires.
research_questions: How many free-text comments does a survey produce, and are they already in one file?
What is the smallest shift crew, and would last year's report have identified them?
Did the last two satisfaction presentations change a management decision, or repeat a story the director already knew?
Will site managers open the Power BI page themselves if the HR business partner stops bringing slides?

role.altitude: The HR business partner moves up from the channel that rule questions pass through to the second line for cases a front door cannot close, and to the person who holds a site manager to day-90 retention, a file that would stand up later, and a grievance that gets an answer. Across Rotterdam, Tilburg, and Venlo they decide which teams are failing the North Star, which is a hire who is productive and still here after 90 days, and what that manager has to change.
reach: The HR administrator's first reading of which contract clause applies, using AFAS and the checklist for what must be in writing.
The payroll specialist's explanation of how a CAO allowance is built up. The month close of payroll stays with payroll.
The recruiter's account of lost offers and slow Recruitee stages, and the briefing of a hiring manager on the structured interview.
The learning and development specialist's chase of forklift, VCA, and food-safety expiries for people already on the roster.
The people-analytics analyst's commentary on the HR dashboard and the first grouping of survey comments. The analyst keeps the model and the nightly AFAS refresh.
role.ceiling_note: Three HR business partners cover three sites in a day window, while about 750 people work shifts and flex headcount swings from about 150 to about 300. These seven tasks are about half the scored year, some 800 of about 1,600 hours. The other half is being on site, the works council, and individual cases, including absence files under the Wet verbetering poortwachter, which do not shrink just because an answer got cheaper. Dismissal files, mediation, and any ranking of people stay with a person. From 2 December 2027, tools that evaluate performance or allocate work from behaviour or traits are high-risk. The works council can refuse a tool that processes personnel data, and IT may allow generative tools only for mail. A Danish study found chatbots saved HR staff about 3 percent of hours on average, so the week changes only where a named task is actually moved.
skills_to_grow: Keep a dated corpus of both CAOs and the house policies, and pull a document when payroll no longer applies it.
Triage a message into a cited answer or a personal file, and keep a dismissal file in a state a person can defend at UWV or the kantonrechter.
Read the Power BI HR dashboard and the Recruitee stages well enough to challenge a figure.
Coach a manager through a hard talk while the manager speaks in their own words.
File a works-council consent request under WOR art. 27 before a tool processes personnel data, and know when a use becomes high-risk under the EU AI Act.
Judge a 90-day pack with the recruiter: time to hire, offer acceptance, week-one onboarding, and who is still here.
role.ambitious_version: The three HR business partners spend their week as the human second line: day-90 retention by team at each site, a practice session for a team lead before a hard talk, and grievances from the night shift that a survey average would have buried. A front door answers cited policy questions for day staff and for the night shift, and, where the agency agrees, for flex leads. They put a team on the HR director's list when new hires are not productive and still here at day 90, and they say what the manager has to change. They do not score people, and the words an employee receives are the manager's.
